title: Planning staff leave and holiday duty rosters
description: A practical guide for Kenyan school principals on planning staff leave fairly and ensuring adequate holiday coverage for boarding schools and ongoing operations.
body:
Staff leave planning, left to informal, ad hoc arrangement, often results in uneven leave allocation, inadequate holiday coverage, and avoidable staff grievances. A structured, fair approach to leave planning — particularly around the long holiday period — prevents these predictable problems.

Starting leave planning early

Waiting until the holiday is imminent to plan staff leave and duty rosters creates unnecessary pressure and reduces staff ability to plan their own personal commitments. Beginning this planning process at least a month before the holiday period gives staff genuine notice and the school adequate time to resolve any coverage gaps.

Fair allocation of leave

Staff who perceive that leave approval depends on personal favour rather than a consistent, transparent process develop legitimate grievances that affect morale. A clear leave policy — how much leave staff are entitled to, how requests are prioritised when multiple staff want the same period, how conflicts are resolved — applied consistently, builds trust in the process even when a specific request cannot be granted.

Holiday duty for boarding schools

Boarding schools require some staff presence during the holiday for security, facility oversight, and emergency response, even with minimal or no students present. A rotating holiday duty roster, planned well in advance and distributed fairly across eligible staff over successive holidays, avoids the resentment that builds when the same staff members are consistently assigned holiday duty.

Fair practice: Maintain a simple record of which staff have taken holiday duty in previous periods, so the rotation can be genuinely balanced over time rather than relying on memory or assumption about who "always" covers holidays.

Documenting leave records accurately

Accurate leave records — properly documented, with balances tracked over the year — prevent disputes about entitlement and provide the documentation needed for TSC compliance purposes. A system where leave is tracked informally or inconsistently creates both administrative risk and genuine staff frustration when records are disputed.

Communicating return dates clearly

Staff should have unambiguous clarity on when they are expected to return before the next term begins, including any preparation period before students arrive. A clear, written communication — not just a verbal mention in a staff meeting that some may have missed — ensures everyone returns with the same understanding.
